review.shorterRouteReview: The existing literal Laurent coefficient map avoids a new analytic Fricke-field embedding and the external KPoleAt/holomorphic-domain machinery for relative transcendence. Taking a Laurent coefficient of a polynomial relation directly yields a polynomial over the original constants. The already proved scalar independence theorem was reviewed; its full basis-coordinate argument is unnecessary for this finite polynomial relation. Native adjoin induction captures the finite coefficient field, and the audited algebraic and transcendental steps replace all source shape assumptions. No incidental generic normalization theorem or proof-limit change is introduced. The existing expanded j-transcendence theorem will be reused for the actual instantiation.
